purpose: Index tradition, ritual, ceremony, mourning, body-care, and cultural-language records without granting the archive ritual authority.
governing_principle: Scene and vocabulary may be indexed; sacred practice, restricted knowledge, community authority, and family decision-making remain outside the archive unless explicitly governed by the relevant people.

clusters.name: Jewish body care and mourning-house language
Muslim bedside, body care, and burial language
Hindu antyeshti and diaspora adaptation language
Buddhist memorial and Tibetan Buddhist high-gate language
Quaker, Orthodox, Sikh, humanist, and secular ceremony language
Home funeral, green burial, Día de los Muertos, and African American funeral-history language

rendering_rule: No record in this atlas may become a public page until named tradition/community review, local-law review where relevant, source-card review, anti-appropriation review, and tone/accessibility review are complete.
nonclaims: not a claim of authority over living communities
not a substitute for clergy, chaplains, elders, celebrants, family wishes, or local law
